land.text: the counties of Troyes, Reims-side Champagne and Langres borderland as Cliopatria draws them in 990

predecessors.note: The pages opened name no count of Troyes before Odo II ('The page does not name any count of Troyes before Odo II'); the infobox says only 'Established: 12th century'. The start is Cliopatria's first year, 990 (confidence 1).

land.text: the county, reunited with the royal domain by Philip IV's marriage to Joan I in 1284

successors.note: Cliopatria's Kingdom of France shape of 1285 holds 106 of the 112 cells of the 1279 Champagne shape. The Crown lands page: reunion in 1284, 'made official in 1361'.

land.text: Champagne and Brie in the royal domain

successors.note: The royal-domain dossier records the 1284 gain from Champagne.

capitals.name: Troyes
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Capital: Troyes'; Henry the Liberal 'later made it the capital and built a palace there'. The page names no earlier seat and no date; under Philip IV the county was ruled from Paris.

keyframe_review.note: 25,388 km2 (113 cells: Troyes, Reims, Rethel, Langres, Bar-sur-Aube, Vitry). The infobox gives no area, so no ratio. The page names no count of Troyes before Odo II and no territory for 990-1020: unverified: page budget.

correction.text: the Cliopatria shape unchanged, valid 1003-1021 only: from 1022 to 1027 the land is drawn in the Blois keyframe county-of-blois_1022 (Odo II count of Troyes and Meaux from 1022)

keyframe_review.note: 27,467 km2 (122 cells): the 990 shape plus a nine-cell block at Sens and Joigny. Valid 1003-1021 only: after Stephen I's death (1019/1020) Odo II of Blois 'seized Troyes, Meaux and all of Champagne for himself' and holds the titles from 1022 (Odo II page); the Champagne page dates the inheritance 1021. From 1022 to 1036 the land is the Blois shape (county-of-blois_1022). The Sens block: the Crown lands page records the 'annexation of the County of Sens' in 1055 and no page opened says Champagne ever held Sens, so the block stays flagged, not removed. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1003..1021 from this entry's own 'Valid 1003-1021 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

minus.text: Provins and Château-Thierry, the Champagne lands Theobald III of Blois kept in 1037

correction.text: Stephen II's counties: Meaux, Troyes, Vitry-le-François and the rest of Champagne without Provins and Château-Thierry

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1037-1039: Odo II died 15 November 1037; 'his brother Stephen inherited the counties of Meaux, Troyes and Vitry-le-François' (Theobald III page), while Theobald III kept Provins, Château-Thierry and St. Florentin. Cliopatria has no Champagne shape for 1028-1039 (the land sits in the Blois shape). Confidence 2: outline from Cliopatria's 1040 Champagne shape minus a radius at Provins and Château-Thierry.

minus.text: Provins and Château-Thierry, the Champagne lands Theobald III of Blois kept in 1037

keyframe_review.note: 27,490 km2 (123 cells), plus one cell near Langres. Provins and Château-Thierry stay with Theobald III of Blois from 1037, so the radius is subtracted for 1040-1055; the Theobald III page does not date his takeover of Odo of Champagne's lands. The Sens block (see 1003) is still in the shape and leaves in 1056, the year after the Crown lands page's 'annexation of the County of Sens' (1055).

minus.text: Provins and Château-Thierry, the Champagne lands Theobald III of Blois kept in 1037

correction.text: Champagne without Provins and Château-Thierry, valid 1056-1062

keyframe_review.note: 25,320 km2 (114 cells), the 1040 shape without the Sens block. Valid 1056-1062 with Provins and Château-Thierry subtracted. The Blois page: Theobald III 'reunited' the divided domains 'in 1063', so 1063-1065 is Blois land (keyframe county-of-blois_1063). Cliopatria's Champagne row then has no shape until 1094.

New keyframe 1089-1093: after Theobald III's death in 1089 the sons divide Blois and Champagne; Odo 'died in 1093, leaving the possessions to his brother Hugh' (Theobald III page); Stephen-Henry took Blois and Chartres in 1089 (Stephen page, seen in the Blois dossier). Cliopatria's Champagne row restarts in 1094; the 1094 shape is used for these years.

25,185 km2 (112 cells), two cells smaller than 1056. Hugh of Troyes is listed 1102-1125 in the infobox; the page says 'By 1100 the youngest, Hugh, inherited Troyes from his father' and that Bar-sur-Aube and Vitry came to him from his mother Adele of Valois by 1100. The row ends in 1125; in 1125 Theobald IV of Blois becomes Count of Champagne (Theobald II page).

25,185 km2. Henry the Liberal (1152-1181) 'expanded the county to include borderland castles, including nine castles on the border of the Holy Roman Empire' and expanded north by agreement with his brother William White Hands, archbishop of Reims; no year or area is given, and Cliopatria's shape does not change. 'Theobald IV bequeaths Champagne to his elder Henry I' (Blois page) in 1152. Marie continued the policy and by 1198 Champagne was 'a cohesive territorial state'.
25,073 km2. Theobald III, Blanche and Theobald IV 'aggressively expanded the comital domain' (undated). The page gives no area; no border event.

25,163 km2. The War of the Succession of Champagne broke into open warfare in 1215 and was settled in 1222 when Theobald IV 'bought out their rights'; no land changed hands. In 1234 Theobald IV also became King of Navarre, a personal union with a separate state, and sold his overlordship of Blois, Sancerre and Châteaudun (undated).
25,342 km2. Theobald V (1256-1270) and Henry III (1271-1274) 'somewhat expanding the comital domain'. Joan I was betrothed to the future Philip IV; the page gives no border change.

25,342 km2, same shape. Joan I married Philip IV in 1284; the county was then ruled from Paris, with the reunion 'made official in 1361' (Crown lands page). Cliopatria's Kingdom of France shape of 1285 holds 106 of its 112 cells.

ledger.note: 990: Cliopatria's County of Champagne begins. The Champagne page names no count of Troyes before Odo II (infobox 'Established: 12th century'); the year is Cliopatria's, not the page's.

region.text: the nine-cell block at Sens and Joigny that Cliopatria adds to Champagne in 1003 and removes in 1056

ledger.note: 1003: a block at Sens and Joigny joins the Champagne shape. No page opened says Champagne held it: the Champagne page is silent on Sens as a territory and the Crown lands page has only the 1055 'annexation of the County of Sens'. Year and land rest on the Cliopatria shapes.

region.text: Troyes, Meaux and all of Champagne

ledger.note: 1022: Odo II of Blois takes Champagne. After Stephen I's death in 1019/1020 he 'seized Troyes, Meaux and all of Champagne for himself without royal approval'; his titles of count of Troyes and Meaux date from 1022 (the Champagne page says 1021, the Blois page Meaux by 1019 and Troyes in 1023).

minus.text: Provins and Château-Thierry, the Champagne lands Theobald III of Blois kept in 1037

ledger.note: 1037: Stephen II inherits Troyes, Meaux and Vitry. 'His brother Stephen inherited the counties of Meaux, Troyes and Vitry-le-François' when Odo II died on 15 November 1037; Theobald III kept Provins, Château-Thierry and St. Florentin.

region.text: the nine-cell block at Sens and Joigny that Cliopatria adds to Champagne in 1003 and removes in 1056

ledger.note: 1055: the block at Sens leaves the Champagne shape. The Crown lands page records 'annexation of the County of Sens' for 1055; that the cells were Champagne's rests on Cliopatria (shape change in 1056).

1063: Theobald III of Blois reunites Blois and Champagne. The Blois page: the divided domains were 'reunited in 1063'; the Theobald III page says he used his nephew's absence 'to gain control over Odo's possessions in Champagne', with no year.

1089: Champagne is divided from Blois again. 'Following Theobald's death in 1089, Philip I, King of France, was able to arrange for Blois and Champagne' to be divided between his sons; Odo 'died in 1093, leaving the possessions to his brother Hugh'.

1125: Theobald IV of Blois becomes Count of Champagne and Brie. He is 'Count of Champagne and of Brie as Theobald II from 1125' (Theobald II page); Hugh of Troyes is listed 1102-1125 in the Champagne infobox (the Champagne article gives Theobald II as 'r. 1120-1152').
1152: Henry the Liberal takes Champagne. 'Theobald IV bequeaths Champagne to his elder Henry I and Blois to his younger brother Theobald V'; Theobald II died 10 January 1152 (Theobald II page).

1284: Joan I marries Philip IV and Champagne joins the royal domain. 'Joan married the king's son in 1284' (Champagne page); Crown lands page: in 1284 the marriage 'led to the reunion', 'made official in 1361'.

1284: the counts of Champagne end. After the marriage 'the county was ruled from Paris' and Philip ruled it 'with a heavy hand'; the nobles' league of 1314 stood down; Champagne was 'fully integrated into the crown lands in 1361'.

wars.name: Louis VII's war against Theobald II of Champagne

zones.text: Champagne, occupied by the royal army, Vitry-le-François captured

wars.outcome: The conflict 'lasted two years (1142-1144)'; Champagne was occupied by the royal army and Vitry-le-François captured. No treaty is on the page.
wars.note: Recorded as a contest in the county-of-blois ledger, because Theobald held Champagne through the Blois shape in these years.

wars.name: War of the Succession of Champagne
belligerents: Erard of Brienne and Philippa of Champagne
wars.outcome: It 'broke into open warfare in 1215' and was 'not resolved until after Theobald came of age in 1222', when he 'bought out their rights for a substantial monetary payment'. No land changed hands.
wars.note: The Champagne page says it devastated the southeastern part of the county in 1218.

wars.name: Baronial invasion of Champagne
wars.outcome: In 1229-1230 Henry II of Bar attacked from the east and Hugh IV of Burgundy from the south; Blanche of Castile intervened to stop the fighting. No land changed hands.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines on the pages opened; Champagne's frontier with the Empire and the bishoprics of Reims, Auxerre and Langres is a ring of castles and homages (Henry the Liberal's nine border castles).

notes: Not settled. (1) Start 990 is Cliopatria's; the pages opened name no count of Troyes before Odo II and the infobox says 'Established: 12th century' (confidence 1). The earlier counts (Herbert, Stephen I) need their own page; the List of counts of Champagne page did not load (url_not_found). (2) Champagne was held by the Counts of Blois 1022-1036, 1063-1088 and 1125-1151 (personal union). Cliopatria has no Champagne shape in 1028-1039, 1066-1093 and 1126-1151 and draws the land inside the Blois shape, so the ledger records the passings as loss/gain with county-of-blois; the Blois dossier carries the mirror events. New keyframes cover 1037-1039 and 1089-1093. (3) Provins and Château-Thierry stay with Blois from 1037 (Theobald III page), a reading that rests on a radius; their later fate is on no page. (4) The nine-cell Sens block (1003-1055) is Cliopatria's; the Crown lands page has only the 1055 annexation of the County of Sens; the royal-domain dossier records the same gain. Whether Champagne ever held Sens is on no page (confidence 1). (5) The pages disagree on Theobald II's reign (Champagne article 1120; Theobald II page 1125) and on Odo II's Champagne (1019, 1021, 1022, 1023). (6) No page dates Henry the Liberal's expansion or the later additions; Cliopatria's shape stays at about 25,000 km2 from 1094 to 1284. The infobox gives no area. (7) Navarre (1234) was a personal union and is not drawn. identity.rulers is left out: the pages give no continuous list (gaps 1037-1102, 1181-1198). (8) Gazetteer names needed: Provins, Château-Thierry (places). Counterpart county-of-sens has no dossier or Cliopatria row and needs one if the Sens block is kept.
